newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gabon ruler sees "anti-French plot" in Africa.
newsitem.headline: Gabon ruler sees "anti-French plot" in Africa.

text.p: Veteran Gabonese President Omar Bongo, in a thinly-veiled attack on the United States, said in an interview published on Wednesday there was a plot to eject France from Africa and destabilise French-speaking countries.

"I think there exists a plot at the moment against Francophone Africa. How else can you explain that the slightest spark in this part of the continent is immediately fanned," Bongo told the French weekly Paris-Match.
He was referring to political violence which has erupted in Congo and the Central African Republic after engulfing Rwanda, Burundi and the former Zaire.

Bongo, whose oil-rich state is the most important bastion of French economic and strategic interests in central Africa, said: "If there is a plot, it is not aimed against Africa but against France. There is an attempt to drive France off the continent."
The president said he was not seeking to incriminate the United States "but it is clear that there are great powers for whom democracy is a dead letter in Africa".

"Francophone countries of Africa have understood the meaning of democracy but that is far from the case for their English-speaking counterparts, where multi-party systems don't exist. Isn't it strange that no voice denounces that state of affairs," he said.
Bongo said the cause of the current instability in central Africa was a battle for the region's mineral wealth.
"The day is not too far away when we will make war on the troublemakers, on all those who seek to interfere in our affairs," he said.
